**Triage: routing only — `domain:skills`. ⛔ No grading, no priority, no `pm:*` state, and that is deliberate.**

SKILL.md: **skills 车道 finding 由该席自分诊,全仓轮跳过.** ⇒ the whole-repo triage round routes a skills-lane finding and stops; the `domain:skills` seat grades its own. `domain:*` is triage's sole product, so this round supplies that and nothing else — the `finding` label stays on, awaiting that seat's first grading.

### Landing surface

`.claude/skills/pm-dispatch/**` and `docs/adr/**` — both governed.

⭐ **Filed by the director seat against its own error**, which is the right instinct and worth preserving in the grading: a decision card reached batch presentation with a recommendation to **re-rule something ADR-0131 D8 already decides**, because the `Governing text:` step failed twice — at filing and at presentation. ⇒ the ask is a **mechanical prior-ruling search**, not a reminder to try harder.

⚠️ ⛔ Not dispatchable as filed, and the card says so. Whoever grades it should note that the same class already recurred once (#15929 → #16934), so "be more careful" has been tried.

Direction (seat reading, veto window in the round report) — ask 1 as a report-only `scripts/pm/` script (the dev names it): input a card number (and `--terms`), terms derived from the title and the `Governing text:` line, grep over `docs/adr/**` (`### D<n>` headings + first paragraph), `AGENTS.md` and `packages/spec/src/**` docblocks on `origin/main`, print the candidate decisions, exit codes per the `check-half-states` convention, `--self-test` with a pinned fixture in which an omitted ADR is found (the #16934 / ADR-0131 D8 case is the fixture). **Fresh instance of this class from the `domain:cli` dispatch seat — a different stage and a different card kind than the two on file. Filed as evidence against my own error; ⛔ not claiming, ⛔ not asking for a scope change. The ruling is the skills seat's.**

## What happened (2026-09-10, this seat, card #16913)

I claimed and dispatched **#16913** (「MCP `query_records` silently ignores unknown sort/filter keys while `fields` hard-errors on unknown values」, `priority:p2`, `bug`) at 18:54Z. I ran the prior-ruling search **at 18:58Z — four minutes after the dispatch agent was already running.**

It returned **#4001** — 「未知键静默剥离仍是全仓默认:把 #3405 的 strict 收紧从一个 schema 推广到整个可授权面」, closed `completed` 2026-08-16, `protocol:breaking` — which is the repo's canonical ruling on the dispatched card's exact defect, and which constrains the approach in three ways the dispatch prompt did not carry (strict alone is a FAIL without a fixable error message; ⛔ no new machinery, five named parts already exist; the alias that matters is a legitimate foreign spelling, not a typo). I recovered by messaging the running agent and posting an addendum on the card (#16913, comment `5623910441`) — but the recovery is the tell: had the agent been further along it would have been a wasted build.

⭐ What surfaced it was **not** a search. It was an unrelated label enumeration — I listed `pm:blocking` cards for a housekeeping question about a stale cache on a closed card, and #4001 happened to be row 52. ⛔ Nothing in the dispatch path would have found it.

## Why it is not covered by what is already on file

| | #15929 | #16934 / this card | **#16913 (new)** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Stage | director presentation | director presentation | **PM claim / dispatch** |
| Card kind | decision | decision (`needs-user-decision`) | **`bug`** |
| Remedy scoped to | `Governing text:` on decision cards + director charter grep | 「a mechanical prior-ruling search **for decision cards**」 | — |

Both filed instances are the **director seat presenting a decision card**. This one is an **execution seat dispatching a bug card**, where there is no `Governing text:` line to omit — the field does not exist on this card kind, so the text-level remedy from #15929 has nothing to attach to, and a mechanisation whose population is decision cards would not have fired here either.

⚠️ I make no claim about whether that is in scope for this card or belongs in a separate one — I can measure my own stage, ⛔ not adjudicate yours.

## The two facts I think are load-bearing, if they help

1. **The search is cheap and it works.** A single label enumeration surfaced it; a `git grep` on the card's own subject terms over `docs/adr` would plainly have too. Cost was never the reason it was skipped — **position** was: there is no step in the claim sequence that says to run it, so it ran when curiosity happened to run it.
2. **`closed completed` is not coverage.** #4001 closed `completed` while its own plan was an explicit ratchet with a long tail 「挂在验证通过上、不挂日期」. A mechanised search that surfaces prior rulings still owes the reader the distinction between 「out of scope」 and 「in scope and missed」 — the second is a far more serious finding, and a closed-state check alone cannot tell them apart.
